title: 1953 AHSME Problem 28
statement: In triangle \(ABC,\) sides \(a,\) \(b\) and \(c\) are opposite angles \(A,\) \(B\) and \(C\) respectively. \(\overline{AD}\) bisects angle \(A\) and meets \(\overline{BC}\) at \(D.\) Then if \(x=CD\) and \(y=BD\) the correct proportion is:

solutions.text:
The angle bisector theorem gives \[ \frac{y}{x}=\frac{c}{b}, \] or \(\frac{y}{c}=\frac{x}{b}.\) Since \(x+y=a,\) \[ \frac yc=\frac xb=\frac{x+y}{b+c}=\frac a{b+c}. \]

Thus, the correct answer is D.
hints: Apply the angle bisector theorem to \(\frac{BD}{DC}\)
